summary_comment: Request and mutation paths are modeled with discriminated unions (`HandleValidation`, `SubmitBanner`), debounced validation with `AbortController` and a sequence counter to drop stale responses, and an in-flight guard plus `submitPhase` for submit. A pure `parseSubmitErrorPayload` keeps error shaping out of the component body, and the Vite plugin splits the demo API into small helpers (`readJsonBody`, `sendJson`, `handleApi`). The React UI is still a single large `App.tsx` (~330 lines) mixing field UI, effects, and fetch orchestration, which is coherent for a demo but not split into smaller units. There is no test runner or `*.test`/`*.spec` coverage in `package.json` or the tree, so important edge cases (422 shape, abort/seq behavior) are not locked in by tests even though some logic is naturally unit-testable.
